title: Social Security, IRS will stay open while other federal workers enjoy an extended holiday
summary: Well, at least they'll have Christmas Day off. But while most other federal workers were given the day before and after Christmas off, the Social Security Administration and the IRS plan to stay open both days.
content:
By Jory Heckman

Well, at least they’ll have Christmas Day off.

But while most other federal workers were given the day before and after Christmas off, the Social Security Administration and the IRS plan to stay open both days.

SSA Commissioner Frank Bisignano told employees in an all-staff email Sunday that the agency will keep field offices and phone lines open on Dec. 24 and Dec. 26, “in line with our commitment to meeting the public need.” Processing centers will also be staffed virtually, and virtual administrative law judge hearings will also be held on those days.

Internal documents obtained by Federal News Network show both SSA and the IRS are looking for volunteers to work these days. “In order to balance the needs of the public and our workforce, we will solicit interest from employees who would like to work on Wednesday and Friday,” Bisignano told employees.

Last week, President Donald Trump signed an executive order giving most federal employees Dec. 24 and Dec. 26 off, the first time in recent years that federal employees have received two additional days off around the holiday. Christmas Day is already a standard federal holiday.

Trump’s order noted that some offices may need to remain open, and that some workers may still need to report for duty for “national security, defense or other public need.”

A former SSA executive told Federal News Network it is “not anywhere near normal” for the agency to remain open during holidays declared by the president.

SSA typically sees a lower volume of calls and field office visits around the holidays, before spiking back up in January. Keeping the agency open these days could reduce the need to reschedule appointments into 2026.

Trump finalizes 1% federal pay raise for 2026, smallest since 2021 — also under Trump

Acting IRS Chief Human Capital Officer David Traynor told employees in a recent memo that the agency “will remain open, allowing employees to continue to work mission-critical efforts.” The agency is also looking for volunteers.

Customer service phone lines will be offline on Dec. 24 and Dec. 26, and taxpayer assistance centers will be closed. But Traynor said “cases will still be worked” during these days, and that IT will be on the clock to provide “break-fix support.”

IRS and SSA employees who volunteer to work those days are eligible for holiday pay.

In addition to being SSA commissioner, Bisignano was also recently appointed CEO of the IRS, reporting directly to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who also serves as acting IRS commissioner.

Neither SSA nor the IRS responded to requests for comment.

SSA volunteers working in field offices and teleservice centers will work onsite. Field offices and phone lines will be staffed from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. local time.

The internal guidance states that a manager or officer-in-charge will be required onsite during these hours. They will receive holiday pay, as well as eight hours of administrative leave for each day worked.

Volunteers in processing centers will work a full eight-hour shift, and are also eligible for holiday pay. Processing center volunteers will need to work a full eight-hour shift, but all work will be done remotely. Bisignano said SSA will ensure “necessary staffing” from IT and facilities will be working both days.

He told employees that keeping SSA open these two days is necessary “to serve the nearly 75 million seniors, disabled Americans, and most vulnerable who rely on us every day.”

“Since my confirmation as commissioner, I have pledged to meet our customers when and where they want to be served — online, on the phone, and in person,” he wrote.

SSA, however, is planning to cut visits to its field offices by half next year. NextGov/FCW first reported on the agency’s plan to reduce field office visits.

SSA also lost about 7,000 employees this year through voluntary incentives, and relocated many of its employees from its headquarters and regional offices to field offices.

Shortly after his Senate confirmation in May, Bisignano told employees that his goal is to make SSA a “digital-first” organization, and to overhaul its website, so that more beneficiaries — primarily retirees and Americans with disabilities — can get their questions answered online, instead of over the phone or in person at field offices.

“We’re never going to be client-first if we’re not digital-first in this era,” he said. “That’s the only way we’re going to win. You’re competing with experiences that people have with Amazon. If I can get something done at Amazon, why can’t I get something done the same way with Social Security? That’s how people think.”

OPM advises agencies to consider reducing senior executive staffing

Before Bisignano took office, SSA under the Trump administration proposed and walked back several plans to limit the agency’s level of phone support. SSA in mid-April launched an AI “anti-fraud” check on all claims filed over the phone, which added an extra three days to processing.

In a separate call, Bisignano said his goal was to get call wait times down to “single digits.” The agency later removed some public data on call wait times from its website.

SSA subject-matter experts told the agency’s inspector general office in a report posted Monday that call metrics added and removed from the website this year “reflected the decisions of its changing leadership and what that leadership believed were the most important metrics for the public.”

The report found SSA served 68 million callers in fiscal 2025, a 65% increase compared to the prior year. But about 25 million calls ended without the caller receiving service — either the caller hung up, or because the phone system could not connect callers to an employee. The agency’s wait time metrics don’t include these abandoned calls or callers who received a busy message.

“The agency improved performance because it used a new telecommunications platform and staff realignments,” the IG’s office wrote. “The new platform increased call volume capacity and expanded self-service and automated options.”

Bisignano said in a statement Monday that the results of the IG audit “come as no surprise to anyone following the historic progress we are making at the agency under President Trump’s leadership.”

“We are serving more Americans at significantly faster speeds than ever before,” he said. “While partisan politicians are attempting to undermine trust of SSA, we are determined to continue improving customer service online, on the phone, and in person at field offices.”
author: Federal News Network
